Oral Order

1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned A.P.P. for the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party no. 2.
2.
The petitioners apprehend their arrest in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 354, 379, 467, 468, 406, 420, 120(B), 504 and 506/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the opposite party no. 2 alleges that her uncle-in-law was issueless, hence, gifted his share of landed property to the opposite party no. 2 measuring 64.25 decimals of land by a registered gift deed dated 17.02.2023, next alleges that she went to the block for Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.70517 of 2024(2) dt.05-10-2024 getting the land mutated in her name where she met the petitioners who assured that the land would be mutated in her name and they will get the work done and, hence, asked for the photo copy of the gift deed, the opposite party no. 2, accordingly, gave the photo copy of the gift deed, next alleges that they also got her signature on some blank papers on the pretext that the same would be used for filing stamp paper for the purposes of court-fee, further when the accused did not get the land mutated in her favour, she filed an Informatory Petition No. 785 of 2024 in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gaya and marked the copy to the concerned police station and the Senior Md. 1 Superintendent of Police, Gaya for initiating action, next alleges that on 29.03.2024 she had gone to see the land and saw the petitioners showing the land to some unknown persons on the pretext that opposite party no. 2 intends to sell the land, on objection they abused and acted inappropriately, but on account of timely intervention of her husband she was saved, further the accused persons showed her husband a copy of an agreement wherein it was recorded that accused persons have given Rs.70 lakhs to her when she has not received a single penny and the agreement was prepared on the same paper which she had signed for the purposes of mutation, Patna High Court CR.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case by the opposite party no. 2.
It is further submitted that opposite party no. 2 after receiving an amount of Rs.70 lakhs has instituted the instant FIR.

It is next submitted that in support of the payment made to the opposite party no. 2, the petitioners have the copy of the agreement which bears the signature of the opposite party no. 2 and her husband.

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party no. 2 rebuts the submissions of the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners and submits that it is asserted and submitted that not a single penny has been received by the opposite party no. 2 from the petitioners.
It is further submitted that it does not appear probable that petitioners would have paid the entire amount of Rs.70 lakhs in cash.

It is next submitted that the nature of work, the petitioners do, does not even remotely suggest that they would have been in a position to pay Rs.70 lakhs on which learned counsel Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.70517 of 2024(2) dt.05-10-2024 appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that petitioners sold their land for entering into the agreement with the opposite party no. 2 whereby an amount of Rs.70 lakhs was paid.
It is also submitted that petitioners have sound financial background and as such they were in a position to pay the amount of Rs.70 lakhs.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that a supplementary affidavit would be filed bringing on record all the sale deeds executed by the petitioners in respect of their land prior to entering into an agreement with the opposite party no. 2 to show that Rs.70 lakhs was paid by the petitioners after selling their land.
It is further submitted that income tax return of the petitioners would also be filed to demonstrate that they are financially sound and could have paid the said amount.

7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party no. 2, at this stage, submits that opposite party no. 2 will also file a counter affidavit bringing on record all the relevant facts which have been argued by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners based on the legal notice sent to the opposite party no. 2 as contained in Annexure-3 series to the anticipatory bail application.
8.
Put up this case on 28.10.2024 within top ten cases.
